_comment: Evals for the forkable skill. Each scenario targets a failure mode observed in real usage, not an imagined one. No runner exists yet - run these by hand in a fresh session with the skill loaded and check expected_behavior. See claude-skill/forkable/SKILL.md.

evals.name: misleading-item-name
evals.query: Review next week's Forkable suggestions against my preferences and tell me what to change.
evals.setup: User prefs include dislikes 'fried' and a note preferring lighter lunches. A suggested day is 'Chicken Goddess' (Carrot Express), whose description is 'Panko-crusted free-range chicken, mozzarella, tomato, red onion, and citrus honey mustard slaw' with ingredientTags including high_carb and gluten.
expected_behavior: Reads the item's description and ingredientTags rather than reasoning from the name alone
Identifies Chicken Goddess as a fried, bread-based sandwich despite the name suggesting a bowl or salad
Recommends swapping it, citing the fried preparation and/or high_carb tag as the reason
Does NOT describe it as a bowl, salad, or light dish
evals.regression_note: An earlier version kept this item and called it 'a light green-goddess chicken bowl' because only name, venue and price were surfaced.

evals.name: add-ons-chosen-not-defaulted
evals.query: Order me the Chicken Goddess for Tuesday.
evals.setup: The item has a required 'Choose Side' group (House Salad $0, Sub for Sweet Potato Fries +$2, Sub for Caesar Salad +$1, No Side $0) and an optional 'Add Side' group with items from $4.99 to $6.99.
expected_behavior: Runs choose with --dry-run before placing anything
Notices the required 'Choose Side' group and states which option it selected
Passes the choice explicitly via --select rather than letting the CLI auto-pick and ignoring the needsChoice warning
Quotes the real total including any surcharge, not just the base price
Waits for explicit confirmation before running the command without --dry-run
evals.regression_note: buildDefaultSelections originally took the cheapest option silently, which could replace a side the user was already paying for.

evals.name: day-with-no-suggestion
evals.query: What am I getting for lunch next week?
evals.setup: Three deliveries exist for the week. Two have a suggested meal; one has meal: null because the user did not enable Forkable suggestions for that day.
expected_behavior: Covers all three delivery days, including the one with meal: null
Treats meal: null as a normal state rather than an error or missing data
Proposes a pick outright for the unsuggested day and says nothing will be auto-ordered there
Distinguishes that proposal from a swap of an existing Forkable suggestion
Does NOT report that suggestions are unavailable or not yet posted
evals.regression_note: The Friday review prompt originally stopped early and reported 'suggestions aren't posted yet' whenever no day had a suggestion.

evals.name: never-invent-delivery-days
evals.query: Pick my meals for next week.
evals.setup: The user's company orders lunch on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday only. `week --next` returns exactly three deliveries.
expected_behavior: Reports exactly the three days that exist, with their real dates
Does NOT assume a Monday-to-Friday week or pad the week to five days
Does NOT relabel the days as Monday through Wednesday
Any summary count uses the real day count as its denominator
evals.regression_note: A tester with three delivery days saw the agent default to a Mon-Wed week and report wrong dates.
